about: T1 recall triggers (repacted-wave-d.md D9.2, D9.6): per skill, the command regexes, URL-host regexes and file globs its own SKILL.md names. Patterns only, never prose. Written from the skills' text on 2026-09-27 BEFORE any D9a moment was replayed. `commands` match a Bash command; `hosts` match the host of any URL in a Bash command or a WebFetch; `globs` match an Edit/Write/Read file path. `why` is the pointer's reason, taken from the skill's description.

postgres-supabase.why: you are touching Postgres or Supabase: catalog checks over grep, grant and anon traps, proving a policy fires

google-workspace.why: you are working with Apps Script or Google Drive/Docs/Sheets APIs: clasp deploy re-pinning, shared drives, quotas

safe-ops.why: you are touching secrets or doing something destructive: env-get instead of source, ignore files, delete by recorded id

shell-tooling-traps.why: shell output may be rewritten or truncated here: rtk, tcount for test counts, macOS tool differences, long jobs

concurrent-agent-git.why: you are changing git state in a tree other agents may share: commit by pathspec, never stash, verify the committed tree

vendor-gotchas.why: you are calling a third-party API with known traps: work trackers, Slack, Jira, Telegram, Apify, ad, affiliate and CRM APIs, Railway

frontend-verification.why: you are building or checking UI: build-only breaks, tokens and theming, layout, and proving the rendered state

stack-traps.why: Node/TypeScript or Python tooling may misbehave here: module resolution, typegen gaps, venvs, vitest mocks

llm-pipeline-patterns.why: an LLM API is a stage here: structured output, caching, provider traps, output validation

memory-hygiene.why: you are writing agent memory: heads and the inbox, correcting a claim in every carrier, index budgets
